left.title: Despite new mandatory mask rules, Trump insists it's everyone's 'personal choice'
left.body: After the city of Jacksonville, Florida, announced that masks will be mandatory for public and indoor locations starting Monday, White House press secretary Kaleigh McEnany would not directly say if President Donald Trump planned to wear one at his acceptance speech at the Republican National Convention. The event, scheduled for August, is expected to bring more than 40,000 people from all over the country to Jacksonville, and while the rules may apply to them, it's likely Trump will exempt himself. left.roundup: Jacksonville, Fla. announced a mandatory face-covering policy in public indoor spaces Monday, beginning at 5 p.m. ET. The city is scheduled to host the 2020 Republican National Convention (RNC) and roughly 40,000 attendees from Aug. 24-27, after it was moved from Charlotte, North Carolina. Reports on all sides of the political spectrum concentrated on public health and COVID-19 coronavirus concerns associated with such an event, as well as the recent debate between politicians and legislators about the need for face-covering mandates. Some coverage from left-rated sources focused on President Donald Trump's reported advocacy for "personal choice" when it comes to wearing masks.

center.title: Jacksonville, new site of the Republican National Convention, adopts mandatory mask policy
center.body: Jacksonville, Florida, is adopting a mandatory mask policy for public gatherings in indoor locations, as well as any other scenario where social distancing isn't feasible. The mandate goes into effect at 5 p.m. on Monday. The news probably won't thrill President Trump, since Jacksonville is the new home to the Republican National Convention. The convention was initially slated to take place in Charlotte, North Carolina, but Trump clashed with the state's Democratic Gov. right.title: RNC Responds To Jacksonville’s Mask Order Ahead Of Convention
right.body: The Republican National Committee (RNC) responded Monday to news that Jacksonville is planning to institute a city-wide mask order stop coronavirus from spreading. The Daily Caller asked the RNC about Jacksonville Mayor Lenny Curry’s mask order which he announced Monday afternoon. The order would require masks to be worn inside.
